hero.title: Library
payoff: Four traditions, eight Foundation readings, four thinkers, seven decision patterns.
Start with a name you were given, a thinker you have heard of, or a decision you would have made differently.
hero.boundary: Nothing in the Library changes your result.

sections.heading: How the pieces fit
sections.intro: Your Foundation result is the headline. Everything else here explains, compares, or challenges it.

sections.heading: The eight Foundation readings
sections.intro: Four ways of explaining world politics, each with two strategic postures.

sections.heading: Variants and blends
sections.intro: A normative orientation changes how a reading weighs order against justice. A blend keeps two explanations active under one posture.

sections.heading: The four traditions
sections.intro: The traditions the Foundation scores against. Each is broader than fourteen questions can capture.

sections.heading: The seven dimensions
sections.intro: What sits behind every reading. A score is a position on this model's scale, not a percentile.

sections.heading: Decision Patterns
sections.intro: Seven authored ways of approaching a hard choice. Compare them; none is assigned to you.

sections.heading: Thinkers
sections.intro: Four thinkers, each read from cited work within a dated window. No thinker is assigned a Foundation reading.

sections.heading: The other questionnaires and exercises
sections.intro: Security, Technology, and AI Governance are their own questionnaires. Perspective Runs put you in another actor's seat. Cases ask for one judgment on a live question.

sections.heading: What is not covered
sections.intro: Four traditions do not cover the field. Feminist, postcolonial, and green approaches are described here and not scored.

hierarchy.label: Your Foundation result
hierarchy.description: The headline reading: one archetype, or a blend of two under the same posture.

hierarchy.label: What explains it
hierarchy.description: Posture, normative orientation, and the closest tradition explain parts of the reading.

hierarchy.label: What sits beside it
hierarchy.description: Security, Technology, AI Governance, Perspective Runs, and Cases each answer their own question.

scoringEvidence.body: Your score comes only from your answers. Thinkers, cases, and decision patterns are editorial material and never feed into it.

lensBands.description: How leverage, position, and timing decide what is possible.
How rules, enforcement, consultation, and restraint make cooperation last.
How public meaning, legitimacy, and shared expectations decide what action can be sustained.
How production, finance, capacity, and dependence narrow practical choice.

normativeAliases.label: Order-first
normativeAliases.description: Starts by protecting coexistence, continuity, and limits on imposed agreement.

normativeAliases.label: Conditional
normativeAliases.description: Treats order and justice claims as conditional on the case, the authority, and the likely consequences.

normativeAliases.label: Justice-first
normativeAliases.description: Starts by asking what protection or obligation is owed beyond settled order.

blendExplanation: A blend appears when two explanations score close together under one posture. It names a family of nearby profiles.

dimensions.description: How much weight rivalry, uncertainty about intentions, and positional competition carry in an explanation.
How far rules, monitoring, and repeated interaction can make cooperation last.
How coalitions, regime type, capacity, and other domestic conditions steer foreign policy.
How legitimacy, recognition, identity, and social meaning define interests and threats.
How production, finance, trade dependence, sanctions, and leverage set the room for action.
Whether the safer strategic instinct is to hold back or to use an available advantage.
How sovereignty, settled order, wider protection, and moral obligation are weighed against each other.

contextBoundary: None of these changes your Foundation result.

contextRecords.title: Security
contextRecords.description: Deterrence, escalation, alliances, and the use of force, decided case by case.

contextRecords.title: Technology
contextRecords.description: Controls, capacity, openness, and strategic dependence, decided case by case.

contextRecords.title: AI Governance
contextRecords.description: Who should be allowed to build, release, and stop powerful AI.

contextRecords.title: Perspective Runs
contextRecords.description: The same questions, answered from another actor's seat.

contextRecords.title: Cases
contextRecords.description: One judgment on a live question, with the record up to a stated date.

coverage.detailsSummary: What the four traditions leave out
coverage.canonNote: The Foundation draws mainly on traditions developed in Anglo-American and Western European International Relations. It does not adjust a score for nationality or culture.
